_comment: Tracked source of the non-numeric text in app/public/data/winner.json (drift/export.py write_winner reads it, so the file can be regenerated from scratch). 'pick' and 'concept_stage' are the pre-registered pick record from the selection step and are kept verbatim.
title: Drift: firmware forensics for science
pitch: Consumer wearables are used as research instruments, and vendors change their step, heart-rate and sleep algorithms in firmware updates, which can make cohort data from before and after an update non-comparable. Drift takes two or more firmware versions of an open-source wearable, finds the code on the metric path, runs each version's algorithm on the same recorded sensor data so the effect is a measured number, and writes a dated data-validity memo for a research team.
how_it_works: Take two or more firmware versions of an open-source wearable (Bangle.js / Espruino, PineTime / InfiniTime). The firmware is open source; the recordings are third-party data that are fetched from their owners, cited and never redistributed.
Locate the code on the metric path, from sensor input to reported metric, and show what changed.
Run differential execution: compile the metric algorithm from each version for the host and feed every version the same recorded raw sensor data.
Write a dated memo for the research team: which date ranges are not comparable, by how much, and a suggested sensitivity check.
